# The fixed-sleep guard cannot see page.waitForTimeout, at any threshold

## Context

Found by the positive control that #19028's AC-3 demanded. That AC exists because a tier with zero current hits has unfalsifiable coverage, so widening the scan to it had to be proved rather than assumed. The control failed, and what it found is larger than the scan root.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-21T11:35Z; no equivalent found.

## The Problem

Two probes, same file, same line, at the head of #19028's branch with the component tier already scanned:

```
await page.waitForTimeout(3000)               ->  guard GREEN, exit 0
await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 3000))   ->  guard RED,   exit 1, site named
```

`buildScripts/util/check-fixed-sleeps.mjs` matches `setTimeout` call shapes only. **Playwright's `page.waitForTimeout` has never been visible to it** — not in the component and e2e tiers it has just started scanning, and not in the unit tier it has scanned since it shipped.

This is not a threshold question. These are waits at or above the guard's own `THRESHOLD_MS = 1000`, inside its own declared scope, that it cannot report:

| tier | `waitForTimeout(n)` where n ≥ 1000 | files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unit | 0 | 0 |
| component | 4 | 2 |
| e2e | 49 | 22 |

**53 sites across 24 files**, and the guard reports `OK` over all of them. Full census at `dev`, top of the distribution:

| sites | delays (ms) | file |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | 2500, 1200, 1000, 1200, 1000, 1200, 1000, 1200 | `e2e/core/RefreshDomCorpseRepro.spec.mjs` |
| 5 | 1000, 1000, 2000, 3000, 3000 | `e2e/rendering/LivePreviewMultiWindow.spec.mjs` |
| 4 | 2500, 1000, 1500, 1500 | `e2e/dashboard/DockAutoHideRevealNL.spec.mjs` |
| 4 | 2000, 1000, 1200, 1200 | `e2e/grid/LockedDnDDuplication.spec.mjs` |
| 3 | 1300 ×3 | `component/menu/List.spec.mjs` |
| 3 | 1000, 5000, 1000 | `e2e/grid/RowPinning.spec.mjs` |
| 3 | 1200, 1600, 1600 | `e2e/grid/RowSlotRemapDuplication.spec.mjs` |
| 3 | 1000, 5000, 2500 | `e2e/grid/ThumbDragPause.spec.mjs` |

The remaining 16 files carry one or two each. Tier split: component 4, e2e 49, unit 0.

**`87.8` seconds if every one elapses** — and the quantifier matters in one direction only. Not every spec is reached in every job, so the figure is an upper bound on a full run rather than a per-run cost. But unlike a failure deadline, **`page.waitForTimeout` is unconditional**: there is no happy path on which it costs nothing. Every site that is reached is paid in full, every time. That is the opposite of the two deadlines dispositioned in #19031, and it is why this population belongs in the guard's accounting rather than outside it.

The practical consequence is that the guard's clean exit reads as "this tree has no unexplained second-scale sleeps", and for the dominant Playwright idiom that has never been what it measured.

## The Architectural Reality

- `buildScripts/util/check-fixed-sleeps.mjs:173` — `if (node.callee?.type !== 'Identifier' || node.callee.name !== 'setTimeout') return NaN;`. `page.waitForTimeout` is a `MemberExpression` callee, so it returns `NaN` and is never a site.
- `:288` — `if (!source.includes('setTimeout') && !source.includes('\\u')) continue;`. A file whose only waits are `waitForTimeout` is skipped **before parsing**, so the AST never sees it. The two narrowings compound.
- `:99` — `JUSTIFICATIONS = ['wall-clock-under-test:', 'out-waits:']`, and `:104` `THRESHOLD_MS = 1000`. Both apply unchanged to whatever shapes the detector admits.
- `buildScripts/util/check-fixed-sleeps-baseline.json` — three entries, all unit `setTimeout` timers under test.

The `{file, text, count}` baseline shape is shape-agnostic, so it can grandfather `waitForTimeout` sites without change.

## The Fix

1. Widen the callee predicate to admit a `MemberExpression` ending in `waitForTimeout`, alongside the bare `setTimeout` identifier. Keep it conservative: match the method name, not an arbitrary receiver, so an unrelated `x.waitForTimeout` on a non-page object is still counted rather than silently exempted.
2. Widen the pre-parse short-circuit at `:288` in the same edit, or the new predicate never runs on the files that need it most. **These two are one change; splitting them ships a matcher that cannot reach its inputs.**
3. Baseline the 53 pre-existing sites so the change is green on arrival, and state the count in the PR. Unlike #19028's three, 53 is past the threshold where dispositioning belongs in the same PR — the baseline is the right mechanism here and burning it down is separate work.
4. Update the module docblock, which currently states this narrowing as deliberate; it stops being true.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — a `page.waitForTimeout(n)` with n ≥ `THRESHOLD_MS` and no justification marker fails the guard, and the same call carrying `out-waits:` or `wall-clock-under-test:` passes.
- [ ] **AC-2** — a spec file containing **only** `waitForTimeout` waits and no `setTimeout` token is parsed rather than skipped. This is its own criterion because the pre-parse short-circuit is a second, independent gate, and satisfying AC-1 alone leaves it closed.
- [ ] **AC-3** — the pre-existing sites are in the baseline, the PR states the counts, and the guard exits 0 on arrival. **Two numbers, two populations, and the ticket originally named only one:** the baseline keys on `{file, text}`, so **53 occurrences collapse into 40 entries** — nine lines are byte-identical repeats inside one file, four of them in `RefreshDomCorpseRepro.spec.mjs` alone. The CLI prints 40 and the census counts 53; both are true and neither is "the number of sites". The PR states entries *and* occurrences.
- [ ] **AC-4** — positive controls in **both** shapes, shown in the PR: an unjustified `waitForTimeout` reds, an unjustified `setTimeout` still reds. The second is the regression control — the existing detector must not be broken by widening it.
- [ ] **AC-5** — the module docblock states which call shapes are matched, replacing the sentence that currently records this narrowing as intended.

## Out of Scope

- **The sub-second threshold.** `THRESHOLD_MS = 1000` stays. The wait that produced this chain — `waitForTimeout(400)` in #19024 — is below it and is still not caught after this ticket. That is a third, separate decision with 385 calls behind it, and it needs its own evidence about what an unexplained sub-second wait costs.
- Burning down the baseline this ticket creates.
- `setInterval`, `requestIdleCallback` and other timing primitives; no incident behind them.

## Avoided Traps

Fixing the callee predicate without the pre-parse short-circuit is the trap, and it is the likelier one because `:173` is where the logic looks like it lives. A file of pure `waitForTimeout` waits never reaches line 173 at all.

The second trap is reading this ticket as "the guard was broken". It was narrow, the narrowing was never written down, and its clean exit was read — by me, in a review — as coverage it did not have. The fix is the matcher; the lesson is that a guard's silence is only as wide as its predicate.

## Related

- #19028 — widened the scan roots; its AC-3 positive control is what found this.
- #19024 — the review that started the chain, whose 400 ms wait remains uncaught after this.

Three spellings, each verified to call the real method with 3000 and each

  page['waitFor\x54imeout'](3000)
  page['waitForTim\eout'](3000)
  page['waitForTime\<newline>out'](3000)

All three were invisible before this. The admission is now any backslash rather
than a whitelist of escape forms -- a conservative superset survives the next
widening, where a partial whitelist has to be rediscovered by a probe. Measured
cost: 338 of 672 spec files parsed rather than 185, whole run 0.37s.

The two halves of the gate now have independent controls: dropping the
waitForTimeout token reds the plain no-token arm alone, reverting backslash to
\u reds the escape arm alone.
